Note::TexAccessor::balance_braces¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::balance_braces() const

Repair Structural Brace Counts Cell By Cell¶

balance_braces() makes the unescaped curly braces in every Text cell structurally balanced. It is useful at a controlled cleanup boundary: for example, after assembling generated fragments or before passing extracted source to a later TeX-aware stage that requires balanced groups.

The scan maintains a nesting depth for each cell. An unescaped { is copied and increases that depth. An unescaped } is copied only when it closes an open group; an unmatched closing brace is discarded. If the scan ends with open groups, one } per remaining level is appended at the end. Backslash escapes are copied as two-byte units, so \{ and \} are literal glyphs and do not participate in the count.

That rule is deterministic and idempotent, but deliberately conservative. It cannot infer where a missing closing brace was intended to occur; it places all required closers at the cell boundary. It does not parse comments, validate command arity, match environments, or decide whether an unmatched closing brace should have had an opening brace inserted earlier. Use it to repair brace structure, not to certify that a document expresses the author’s intended TeX.

The result owns fresh Text storage and preserves the receiver’s rank, shape, cell order, and encoding. Empty cells remain empty. Undefined propagates as undefined. Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject rather than being decoded or formatted implicitly. Runtime is linear in the total number of input bytes, with one pass and output proportional to input plus appended closers.

Example 1: Missing Opens, Missing Closes, Escapes, And Valid Input¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    {"{a{b}", "a}}b", R"(\{literal\})", "already {balanced}"});
std::cout << source.tex().balance_braces() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["{a{b}}", "ab", "\\{literal\\}", "already {balanced}"]

The first cell receives one trailing closer. The second loses both unmatched closers, while the escaped braces in the third cell remain literal text.

Example 2: Repaired Text Is A Fixed Point¶

const auto repaired = source.tex().balance_braces();
const bool idempotent =
    (repaired.tex().balance_braces() == repaired).all().bool_item();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "idempotent=" << idempotent
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().balance_braces().defined()
          << '\n';

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false

Example 3: Native Integer Cells Are Not Coerced To Text¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().balance_braces();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "braces Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

braces Int64: rejected
